question: In the BatPaC comparison, how much lower are the total pack cost and the material cost with Co-free cathodes than with NCA cathodes?

SELECT (SELECT CAST(replace(regexp_extract(text,'\$([0-9 ]+) total',1),' ','') AS INT) FROM atoms WHERE id='p3.L19') - (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'\$([0-9]+) total',1) AS INT) FROM atoms WHERE id='p3.L18') AS pack_diff, (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'\$([0-9]+) material',1) AS INT) FROM atoms WHERE id='p3.L20') - (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'\$([0-9]+) material',1) AS INT) FROM atoms WHERE id='p3.L18') AS material_diff

rendered: With Co-free cathodes, the BatPaC analysis gives a total pack cost of $8500 total pack cost, $3500 material costs[1] . With NCA cathodes the comparison gives $10 000 total pack[2] and $5000 material cost[3]. So the total pack cost with Co-free cathodes is lower by $1,500[4] per pack, and the material cost is lower by $1,500[5] per pack. Both reductions are the same size. These figures are from the cost projections in Fig. 2[6].
